claim: The hippocampus plays an important role in spatial processing and episodic memory.
source: The hippocampus plays an important role in spatial processing and episodic memory (Andersen et al., 2006; Tulving, 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to Andersen et al., 2006 and Tulving, 2002

claim: Place cells in the hippocampus sparsely encode location within an environment.
source: Spatial processing and navigation are supported by spatially tuned cells throughout the hippocampal formation, such as place cells in the hippocampus, which sparsely encode location within an environment (O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971; Muller and Kubie, 1987).
evidence: Supported by citations to O'Keefe and Dostrovsky, 1971 and Muller and Kubie, 1987

claim: Time cells have been discovered in the hippocampus.
source: Subsequent discovery of time cells in the hippocampus (Kraus et al., 2013; Pastalkova et al., 2008; MacDonald et al., 2011; Tsao et al., 2018; Rueckemann et al., 2021), which encode time within an episode, suggests that the latter may contribute to the building blocks of episodic memory formation.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations including Kraus et al., 2013; Pastalkova et al., 2008; MacDonald et al., 2011; Tsao et al., 2018; Rueckemann et al., 2021

claim: Time cells encode time within an episode.
source: Subsequent discovery of time cells in the hippocampus (Kraus et al., 2013; Pastalkova et al., 2008; MacDonald et al., 2011; Tsao et al., 2018; Rueckemann et al., 2021), which encode time within an episode, suggests that the latter may contribute to the building blocks of episodic memory formation.
evidence: Supported by citations to studies on time cells

claim: Time cells may contribute to the building blocks of episodic memory formation.
source: Subsequent discovery of time cells in the hippocampus (Kraus et al., 2013; Pastalkova et al., 2008; MacDonald et al., 2011; Tsao et al., 2018; Rueckemann et al., 2021), which encode time within an episode, suggests that the latter may contribute to the building blocks of episodic memory formation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on inference from the discovery of time cells

claim: Time cells and place cells share many physiological properties.
source: Time cells and place cells share many physiological properties, pointing to a unifying concept of the role of the hippocampus in encoding features required to organize relevant information.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge without specific citation in this sentence

claim: Six rats were trained to run on a treadmill in the central stem of a figure-8 maze.
source: In these experiments, six rats were trained to run on a treadmill in the central stem of a figure-8 maze (Figure 1a).
evidence: Describes the experimental setup from Kraus et al., 2013 data

claim: Rats were provided with a small water reward prior to the initiation of the treadmill session and upon its cessation.
source: The rats were provided with a small water reward prior to the initiation of the treadmill session and upon its cessation, thereby conditioning them to maintain their snouts positioned at the water port throughout the duration of the treadmill run, and "clamping" their behavior and spatial position.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure from the Kraus et al., 2013 study

claim: Each session consisted of 31–57 runs.
source: In each session, consisting of 31–57 runs, the treadmill was operated either for a fixed time or for a fixed distance, where in each run the velocity was set to a randomly chosen speed in the range of 35–49 cm/s (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: Describes experimental parameters from the data

claim: The treadmill velocity was set to a randomly chosen speed in the range of 35–49 cm/s in each run.
source: In each session, consisting of 31–57 runs, the treadmill was operated either for a fixed time or for a fixed distance, where in each run the velocity was set to a randomly chosen speed in the range of 35–49 cm/s (Figure 1b and c).
evidence: Describes experimental parameters from the data

claim: Three of the six rats were trained and recorded exclusively in fixed-distance or fixed-time sessions.
source: Three of the six rats were trained and recorded exclusively in fixed-distance or fixed-time sessions, while the remaining three rats were trained and recorded in sessions of both types.
evidence: Describes the experimental design

claim: Three rats were trained and recorded in sessions of both fixed-distance and fixed-time types.
source: Three of the six rats were trained and recorded exclusively in fixed-distance or fixed-time sessions, while the remaining three rats were trained and recorded in sessions of both types.
evidence: Describes the experimental design

claim: Kraus et al. reported that some cells preferentially encoded the distance the rat had run on the treadmill.
source: Kraus et al. reported that some cells preferentially encoded the distance the rat had run on the treadmill, while other cells preferentially encoded the time from the start of the treadmill movement.
evidence: References findings from Kraus et al. study

claim: Kraus et al. reported that some cells preferentially encoded the time from the start of the treadmill movement.
source: Kraus et al. reported that some cells preferentially encoded the distance the rat had run on the treadmill, while other cells preferentially encoded the time from the start of the treadmill movement.
evidence: References findings from Kraus et al. study

claim: Of 930 cells recorded, 679 cells with at least 10 runs showing firing peaks greater than 0.5 Hz were analyzed.
source: Of 930 cells recorded we analyzed 679 cells with at least 10 runs showing firing peaks greater than 0.5 Hz.
evidence: Describes the data analysis parameters

claim: Only cells with peak firing rates occurring during the treadmill run were included in the analysis.
source: Only cells with peak firing rates occurring during the treadmill run were included in the analysis.
evidence: Describes inclusion criteria for analysis

claim: Both distance cells and time cells were observed in the study.
source: As previously reported in Kraus et al., 2013, we observed both distance cells, showing a response at constant distances the animal traveled on the treadmill, and time cells, showing a response at constant times from the treadmill start (Figure 2).
evidence: Describes observations from the data analysis, with reference to Figure 2

claim: In fixed-distance sessions, 67% of neurons were distance cells.
source: In fixed-distance sessions, the neurons exhibited a significant majority (67%) of distance cells.
evidence: Reports quantitative finding from data analysis

claim: In fixed-time sessions, 68% of neurons were time encoding cells.
source: By contrast, in fixed-time sessions time encoding cells dominated (68%).
evidence: Reports quantitative finding from data analysis

claim: Of the 444 neurons recorded in fixed-distance sessions, 298 cells were classified as distance cells and 146 as time cells.
source: Of the 444 neurons recorded in fixed-distance sessions, the CellType index classified 298 cells as distance cells and 146 as time cells (Figure 3a).
evidence: Reports specific counts from data analysis

claim: In fixed-time sessions, 76 of 235 neurons were classified as distance cells and 159 of 235 were classified as time cells.
source: Conversely, in the fixed-time sessions 76 of 235 neurons were classified by this index as distance cells and 159 of 235 were classified as time cells.
evidence: Reports specific counts from data analysis

claim: The relation between the cell type and the experiment type is significant (χ2(1)=75.1, p>>0.001 for the total cell population).
source: The relation between the cell type and the experiment type is significant (χ2(1)=75.1, p>>0.001 for the total cell population).
evidence: Reports statistical test results from the data analysis

claim: In 5 out of 6 animals, the cells' encoding depended on the session type.
source: In 5 out of 6 animals, the cells' encoding depended on the session type (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). (χ2(1)>12, p<<0.001 for 4 animals, χ2(1)=5.7, p<0.02 for one animal), except in one animal (χ2(1)=2.38, p=0.12).
evidence: Reports statistical findings from per-animal analysis

claim: The optimal threshold for classification of a session based on the CellType metric was 0.
source: We found that the optimal threshold (maximum Youden index) for classification of a session based on the CellType metric, was 0.
evidence: Reports finding from ROC analysis

claim: The threshold of 0 classifies 67% of the cells as Distance in the Distance sessions and only 32% on the Time sessions.
source: This threshold classifies 67% of the cells as Distance in the Distance sessions and only 32% on the Time sessions.
evidence: Reports classification performance metrics

claim: The dimension the cells encode (Time vs. Distance) is related to the session type (fixed time vs. fixed distance).
source: These results indicate that the dimension the cells encode (Time vs. Distance) is related to the session type (fixed time vs. fixed distance).
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the statistical analyses and shuffle test

claim: In experiments where the treadmill running-time was fixed, the majority of cells encoded a given time from treadmill onset.
source: In experiments where the treadmill running-time was fixed, the majority of cells encoded a given time from treadmill onset.
evidence: Summary of main finding from the analysis

claim: In experiments where the treadmill running-distance was fixed, the majority of cells encoded a specific accumulated distance from treadmill onset.
source: In contrast, in experiments where the treadmill running-distance was fixed, the majority of cells encoded a specific accumulated distance from treadmill onset.
evidence: Summary of main finding from the analysis

claim: Accumulated time in fixed-time experiments and accumulated distance in fixed-distance experiments may be used as predictors for the progress of the rat towards anticipated reward.
source: It is worth noting that accumulated time in fixed-time experiments and accumulated distance in fixed-distance experiments may be used as predictors for the progress of the rat towards anticipated reward, which is given at the end of the treadmill run (Whittington et al., 2020; Stachenfeld et al., 2017).
evidence: Interpretive statement supported by citations

claim: The same cells which showed distance-encoding and time-encoding properties in the treadmill were often selective to places outside of the treadmill as well.
source: As noted previously in Kraus et al., 2013 the same cells, which showed distance-encoding and time-encoding properties in the treadmill, were often selective to places outside of the treadmill as well.
evidence: References finding from Kraus et al., 2013

claim: CA1 pyramidal cells can encode location, distance, or time, depending on the conditions of the experiment or task demand.
source: To summarize, CA1 pyramidal cells can encode location, distance, or time, depending on the conditions of the experiment or task demand.
evidence: Summary conclusion based on the findings of the study

claim: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for diverse parameter spaces, such as auditory linear frequency.
source: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for diverse parameter spaces, such as auditory linear frequency (Aronov et al., 2017), social mapping (Omer et al., 2018; Schafer and Schiller, 2018) or more abstract spaces (Constantinescu et al., 2016; Retailleau and Morris, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Aronov et al., 2017

claim: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for social mapping.
source: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for diverse parameter spaces, such as auditory linear frequency (Aronov et al., 2017), social mapping (Omer et al., 2018; Schafer and Schiller, 2018) or more abstract spaces (Constantinescu et al., 2016; Retailleau and Morris, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Omer et al., 2018 and Schafer and Schiller, 2018

claim: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for more abstract spaces.
source: Consistency with task demands has been repeatedly demonstrated in hippocampal recording for diverse parameter spaces, such as auditory linear frequency (Aronov et al., 2017), social mapping (Omer et al., 2018; Schafer and Schiller, 2018) or more abstract spaces (Constantinescu et al., 2016; Retailleau and Morris, 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Constantinescu et al., 2016 and Retailleau and Morris, 2018

claim: The activity of place cells and grid cells is commonly modeled using continuous attractor networks.
source: The activity of place cells and grid cells is commonly modeled using continuous attractor networks (Morris and Derdikman, 2023; Samsonovich and McNaughton, 1997; Burak and Fiete, 2009; Fuhs and Touretzky, 2006; Bush and Burgess, 2014; Hasselmo and Brandon, 2012; Tocker et al., 2015; Gu et al., 2018; Geiller et al., 2022; O'Keefe and Burgess, 1996).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to modeling studies

claim: Continuous attractor networks may serve as a natural substrate for amplification of encoding of certain task features, at the expense of others, resulting in an over representation of the salient variables.
source: Such networks may serve as a natural substrate for amplification of encoding of certain task features, at the expense of others, resulting in an over representation of the salient variables.
evidence: Theoretical speculation about mechanism

claim: Over-representation of salient variables may help the brain prioritize survival and decision making.
source: Such over-representation may help the brain prioritize survival and decision making.
evidence: Speculative statement about functional significance

claim: By allocating more resources to the salient stimuli, the brain enhances the ability to process and retain the important information.
source: By allocating more resources to the salient stimuli, the brain enhances the ability to process and retain the important information.
evidence: General principle based on established neuroscience knowledge

claim: The hippocampus is adaptive in its cells' encoding and seems to be capable to tune them to the parameters best describing the task.
source: Irrespective of the exact mechanism explaining the results of this study, the hippocampus is adaptive in its cells' encoding and seems to be capable to tune them to the parameters best describing the task.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the study findings

claim: Response onset for each neuron and run was defined as the first bin, following at least 1 s of silence within a series of consecutive bins with firing activity which includes the peak of firing.
source: Response onset for each neuron and run, was defined as the first bin, following at least 1 s of silence within a series of consecutive bins with firing activity which includes the peak of firing.
evidence: Describes methodological definition used in analysis

claim: The peak firing was defined as the bin with the highest value within a run.
source: The peak firing was defined as the bin with the highest value within a run, however only cells with an average peak firing of at least 0.5 Hz were included.
evidence: Describes methodological definition used in analysis

claim: The treadmill moving times were divided into 100ms time bins.
source: We divided the treadmill moving times into 100ms time bins (other bin resolutions between 50 ms and 500 ms were tested and provided similar results).
evidence: Describes analysis methodology

claim: Other bin resolutions between 50 ms and 500 ms were tested and provided similar results.
source: We divided the treadmill moving times into 100ms time bins (other bin resolutions between 50 ms and 500 ms were tested and provided similar results).
evidence: Reports robustness check of methodology

claim: The analysis was extended to 5 s past the treadmill stop time to ensure the activity peak is not missed.
source: To ensure the activity peak is not missed, we extended the analysis to 5 s past the treadmill stop time.
evidence: Describes methodological choice

claim: The distributions of peak firing rates and average firing rates for time cells and distance cells were similar.
source: Our findings revealed that the distributions of peak firing rates and average firing rates, for time cells and distance cells, were similar (see Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Reports finding from additional analysis

claim: Time cells were initially reported in animals running on a running wheel without control of velocity.
source: Time cells were initially reported in animals running on a running wheel without control of velocity (Pastalkova et al., 2008, although time cells were also reported for immobile rats MacDonald et al., 2011).
evidence: Historical context supported by citations

claim: Time cells were also reported for immobile rats.
source: Time cells were initially reported in animals running on a running wheel without control of velocity (Pastalkova et al., 2008, although time cells were also reported for immobile rats MacDonald et al., 2011).
evidence: Historical context supported by citation to MacDonald et al., 2011

claim: Kraus et al., 2013 varied the velocity of rats running in place on a treadmill.
source: Kraus et al., 2013 varied the velocity of rats running in place on a treadmill, and found subpopulations of hippocampal cells that encoded time, other cells that encoded path-integrated distance and additional cells that encoded both time and distance.
evidence: Describes experimental design from cited study

claim: Kraus et al., 2013 found subpopulations of hippocampal cells that encoded time.
source: Kraus et al., 2013 varied the velocity of rats running in place on a treadmill, and found subpopulations of hippocampal cells that encoded time, other cells that encoded path-integrated distance and additional cells that encoded both time and distance.
evidence: Reports findings from cited study

claim: Kraus et al., 2013 found cells that encoded path-integrated distance.
source: Kraus et al., 2013 varied the velocity of rats running in place on a treadmill, and found subpopulations of hippocampal cells that encoded time, other cells that encoded path-integrated distance and additional cells that encoded both time and distance.
evidence: Reports findings from cited study

claim: Kraus et al., 2013 found additional cells that encoded both time and distance.
source: Kraus et al., 2013 varied the velocity of rats running in place on a treadmill, and found subpopulations of hippocampal cells that encoded time, other cells that encoded path-integrated distance and additional cells that encoded both time and distance.
evidence: Reports findings from cited study

claim: The type of experimental condition significantly influenced the encoding of hippocampal cells.
source: Our findings indicate that the type of experimental condition significantly influenced the encoding of hippocampal cells.
evidence: Main conclusion from the study's analysis

claim: Distance-encoding cells dominated in fixed-distance experiments.
source: Specifically, distance-encoding cells dominated in fixed-distance experiments, whereas time-encoding cells dominated in fixed-time experiments.
evidence: Main finding from the study

claim: Time-encoding cells dominated in fixed-time experiments.
source: Specifically, distance-encoding cells dominated in fixed-distance experiments, whereas time-encoding cells dominated in fixed-time experiments.
evidence: Main finding from the study

claim: The flexible coding capabilities of the hippocampus are shaped by over-representation of salient variables associated with reward conditions.
source: These results underscore the flexible coding capabilities of the hippocampus, which are shaped by over-representation of salient variables associated with reward conditions.
evidence: Interpretive conclusion from the study findings

claim: The rats were forced to alternate their post-treadmill turns between right and left.
source: The rats were forced to alternate their post-treadmill turns between right and left.
evidence: Describes experimental procedure

claim: All experiments were truncated to 16 s in order to prevent biases in the shuffle distribution analysis.
source: In order to mitigate any potential biases in this distribution, we truncated all data to a common duration of 16 s, which represents the shortest duration of a treadmill run across all sessions.
evidence: Describes methodological choice for statistical analysis

claim: 16 s represents the shortest duration of a treadmill run across all sessions.
source: In order to mitigate any potential biases in this distribution, we truncated all data to a common duration of 16 s, which represents the shortest duration of a treadmill run across all sessions.
evidence: Describes property of the experimental data

claim: For ideal time cells, firing should be independent of running speed.
source: Our classification method is based on the premise that for ideal time cells, firing (and hence onset time) should be independent of running speed.
evidence: Describes theoretical basis for classification method

claim: An ideal distance cell would display firing onsets at times depending on the speed.
source: Conversely, an ideal distance cell would display firing onsets at times depending on the speed.

claim: Basing the analysis on peak values instead of onset yielded comparable results and levels of statistical significance.
source: Basing our analysis on the peak values instead yielded comparable results and levels of statistical significance (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
